subject: Privately-deployed fleet — stability slate & reversion timeline
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.ai>
To: Alex R. <ops_lead@acmehealth.com>, Samira Patel <samira.patel@edgecloud-partner.net>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Privately-deployed fleet — stability slate & reversion timeline

Hi Alex / Samira —

Following our call last week, I put together a short stability slate and proposed reversion timeline for the private deployment upgrade scheduled for the week of Jun 21. Primary goals: limit blast radius, make automated reversion possible within 15 minutes, and preserve KV cache integrity for live sessions.

High level proposal (see attached stability_matrix.xlsx):
- Pin window: only fleet slice 2027-06-21 02:00–06:00 UTC (narrow window)
- Canary rollout: 5% initial, 20% after 30m stable telemetry, full ramp at 3h
- Reversion target: automated reversion to prior pinned version with traffic cutover within 15 min if any of the gating metrics cross thresholds (detailed below)
- DB migrations: none planned in this release; if required, will be separated into a separate deploy.

Gating/abort criteria (examples):
- Latency P95 increase > 120% baseline over 10m
- Error rate (5xx) > 1% sustained for 5m
- Mean token generation throughput drop > 30% for 10m

Roles and bridge plan:
- Redwood oncall (Karthik) runs the release bridge and executes rollback choreography if asked
- Customer ops (Alex) to validate telemetry and confirm business-facing incidents
- Partner network (Samira) to monitor interconnect and announce any region-level anomalies

Requested actions by EOD Friday:
1) Alex — confirm the window & narrow-slice preference or propose alternate slot
2) Samira — confirm network capacity checks and if you require an extended preflight window
3) Karthik/Jonas/Neha — review the attached preflight checklist and call out missing revert hooks

Attachments: stability_matrix.xlsx, preflight-checks.txt

Thanks —
Maya Srinivasan
Engineering Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Alex R. <ops_lead@acmehealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privately-deployed fleet — stability slate & reversion timeline

Maya —

Thanks for the clear plan. Jun 21 window works for us (02:00–06:00 UTC is fine). A couple of quick asks from Acme ops:
- Can you include a short snapshot of audit logs (preflight) that our compliance team can retain? A CSV export of recent access/ops would be ideal.
- While you noted no DB migrations, we do need to confirm there are no schema-affecting model metadata writes during the rollout; please confirm whether model version pins touch our metadata store.

We also want an explicit SLA fallback: if we detect any customer-facing degradation we will ask for immediate freeze and rollback at the 20% or 3h markers — confirm that Redwood can execute automated revert and that the previous KV snapshots remain valid.

If you can send the audit export and a one-paragraph confirmation on metadata writes, I'll escalate to compliance and sign off.

Cheers,
Alex R.
Head of Platform Ops — AcmeHealth
ops_lead@acmehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.s@redwood.ai>, Alex R. <ops_lead@acmehealth.com>, Samira Patel <samira.patel@edgecloud-partner.net>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privately-deployed fleet — stability slate & reversion timeline

Thanks Maya — adding technical details and gating automation notes.

Summary: Redwood can perform an automated revert to the pinned prior version; the revert process does the following in sequence (rollback_playbook.md attached):
1) Mark new variant draining: stop new container allocations and begin draining connections from the 5% slice
2) Restore previous model binary (pinned artifact) to canary nodes (fast-path cache warmup)
3) Apply KV cache warmup using saved snapshots; if snapshot restore fails, we fall back to cold-start with graceful 503 ramp for affected sessions
4) Re-route traffic at the LB layer and validate success via health-checks + traffic shadowing for 5m

Preflight notes:
- We will produce an audit_log_snapshot.csv (sanitized) and drop it in the Drive link.
- Metadata writes: this release is read-only for model-pinning metadata; we do not perform schema migrations. The model pin operation updates a small reference pointer in our control plane, which is transactional and has a rollback path.

Gating automation (implemented in infra):
- Automatic abort if P95 latency > 120% baseline for 10m OR 5xx > 1% for 5m — triggers revert workflow automatically and pages oncall.
- If automated abort fails, manual abort button on the bridge instructs netops (Samira) to cut new traffic.

Attachments: rollback_playbook.md, preflight-checks.txt

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Alex / Samira —

Thanks for the quick replies and the questions. To confirm explicitly for compliance:
- We will provide audit_log_snapshot.csv (sanitized) to AcmeHealth via the linked Drive folder before the preflight window.
- No schema or DB migrations in this release; model pin updates a control-plane reference only and is fully reversible.
- Automated revert is in place and validated on our staging fleet; full revert takes <15 mins in our tests (typical: 7–10m to warm prior caches + LB cutover).

I scheduled a 30m bridge dry-run next Wed (2027-06-09 17:00 UTC) to run the rollback procedure end-to-end with your team. Please RSVP if you or someone from Acme compliance wants to join.
